title: Angiomatous meningioma with bizarre nuclei: A case report
case_prompt:
A 45-year-old woman presented with intermittent left-sided headache of >1 year’s duration. The pain lasted minutes to an hour, was sometimes accompanied by nausea and vomiting, and improved with rest. There was no history of dizziness, visual disturbance, seizures, sensory changes, or focal neurologic deficits, and the physical examination was unremarkable. 

Brain MRI revealed a dural-based soft-tissue mass in the right frontal lobe. The lesion was surgically excised. On gross examination, the formalin-fixed specimen measured 2.0 × 2.0 × 0.8 cm, was gray-white, smooth, and attached to the dura mater.

Microscopic examination showed a network of dense small vessels and thick-walled larger vessels, most with marked hyalinization, interwoven throughout the lesion. In focal areas, a faint “whirlpool-like” arrangement of tumor cells was noted. Scattered cells exhibited bizarre, large, hyperchromatic, and irregularly distributed nuclei. No mitotic figures were identified.

Immunohistochemical studies demonstrated that the tumor cells were strongly positive for Vimentin and SSTR2A, with focal positivity for EMA and partial positivity for progesterone receptor. CD34 and ERG highlighted only the vascular endothelium, with no staining in tumor cells. GFAP, Olig-2, and HMB45 were negative. The MIB-1 (Ki-67) labeling index was less than 3%.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Prominent vascular channels with hyalinization and focal meningioma-type whorls support angiomatous meningioma — “dense small vessels ... and thick-walled large vessels ... interwoven to form a vascular network ... The whirlpool-like structure of meningioma was faintly seen”.  
2. Immunoprofile with Vimentin+, SSTR2A+, and EMA+ in tumor cells confirms meningioma lineage — “Immunohistochemically, the meningeal epithelial cells were strongly positive for Vimentin and SSTR2A ... and EMA was focally positive”.  
3. Absence of mitoses and a low Ki-67 index exclude higher-grade (grade II/III) meningioma — “No mitotic figures were observed ... the cells did not differ with regard to proliferative activity and mitotic imaging. Therefore ... did not meet grade II meningioma and even grade III meningioma criteria.”  
4. Angiosarcoma is excluded based on immunophenotypic differences — “Differential diagnoses of AM include ... vasogenic tumour, especially angiosarcoma ... These tumours can be well identified by immunophenotype.”  
5. Hemangioblastoma is excluded based on immunophenotypic differences — “Differential diagnoses of AM include ... hemangioblastoma ... These tumours can be well identified by immunophenotype.”  
6. Solitary fibrous tumour and malignant melanoma are excluded by negative GFAP, Olig-2, and HMB45 and by immunophenotype — “others, such as solitary fibrous tumours (SFTs) and malignant melanoma. These tumours can be well identified by immunophenotype.”
